name: DroidLink v3.7 Stable
body:
# DroidLink v3.7 Stable

DroidLink v3.7 combines the streaming, controller, network-recovery, and compatibility work validated throughout the v3.6.x development cycle.

## Important installation notice

This release begins a new permanent DroidLink signing identity. Android cannot update an APK signed by the previous identity.

If DroidLink v3.6 or an older build is installed, uninstall it once before installing v3.7. Local DroidLink settings will be reset. After v3.7 is installed, Obtainium can install future updates normally as long as those releases use this same v3.7 signing identity.

## Streaming

- Preserves the tested Auto and Balanced modes.
- Improves Low Latency behavior under heavy-game encoder pressure.
- Reduces severe resolution and FPS collapse.
- Drops stale work before encoding to limit progressive latency buildup.
- Keeps bounded WebRTC adaptation and recovery hysteresis.
- Removes High Quality and safely migrates its old stored preference to Auto.

## Controllers

- Preserves physically tested built-in, Bluetooth, and mixed-controller configurations.
- Supports standard Android GAMEPAD and JOYSTICK devices, including compatible USB controllers.
- Protects controller assignment, analog controls, triggers, D-pad, buttons, and multiplayer ordering.
- Improves controller disconnect/reconnect state cleanup without changing the working packet format.

## Network reliability

- Detects active Android network loss and network changes.
- Allows normal WebRTC recovery before a bounded ICE restart.
- Limits recovery attempts and prevents duplicate PeerConnections, media encoders, or controller channels.
- Keeps direct connections preferred and TURN available as fallback.
- Preserves the existing Firebase schema, room structure, and signaling contract.
- Adds safe network and recovery diagnostics without exposing credentials or IP addresses.

## Compatibility and stability

- Adds Android 10-safe display refresh-rate handling.
- Prevents released renderers from accumulating across repeated sessions.
- Rechecks playback-capture permission immediately before audio initialization.
- Clears signaling, renderer, audio, ICE, callback, and retry state during session teardown.
- Preserves the current audio, multiplayer, profile, room-code, and user-interface architecture.

## Validation

- Clean release build completed.
- Unit tests passed.
- Android release lint passed.
- Release APK signature verified.
- Release APK is not debuggable.
- Auto, Balanced, and Low Latency are the only selectable presets.

Restrictive/public Wi-Fi behavior remains pending additional field validation. Network and playback-audio behavior may vary according to device, game capture policy, NAT, firewall, and Wi-Fi restrictions.

APK SHA-256: `bee18c4908112be559377660bbdaeee5d33a89e29a4f90b3a778f5decd06178b`

name: DroidLink 3.6 Stable
body:
DroidLink 3.6 establishes a stable multiplayer and update baseline.

Reliability fixes:
- Restores Firebase Realtime Database signaling with an explicit database URL.
- Stores Firebase configuration and scoped six-digit room rules with the source.
- Uses the verified Cloudflare TURN Worker with credentialed UDP, TCP, and TLS relay URLs.
- Retries TURN credential requests three times.
- Falls back to three independent STUN endpoints when TURN is temporarily unavailable.
- Keeps the listener-based offer flow that avoids the host/join signaling race.

Release integrity:
- Version 3.6 (version code 39).
- Signed with DroidLink's permanent release key for compatible future updates.
- Unit tests, release lint, APK signature, Firebase access, and live TURN response verified.
- Automatic rotating debug-key GitHub releases are disabled.

Install this same 3.6 APK on every participating device. Because older builds and the 3.5.1 test used different signing keys, one uninstall may be required before installing 3.6. Future stable updates signed with the 3.6 key can update in place.

APK SHA-256:
6ad94a976a8ea644897ab226e4b379d2aaafeb21ec696721fccd5a31d0babf3d

# DroidLink v3.5 — Release Notes

DroidLink v3.5 continues the push toward a more stable, polished, and reliable Android-to-Android gaming experience. This release focuses heavily on multiplayer stability, controller reliability, streaming quality, and overall cleanup.

### What’s New & Improved

- **Improved Multiplayer Stability**
  - Better handling of multiple connected players.
  - Players now maintain their correct join order during a session.
  - Improved player connection/disconnection handling.

- **Controller Stability Improvements**
  - Additional fixes aimed at preventing controllers from dropping during longer gaming sessions.
  - Improved reliability with **Winlator**.
  - Continued controller compatibility improvements across supported games and emulators.
  - Preserves the controller system that proved stable during previous DroidLink testing.

- **Streaming & Video Improvements**
  - Additional work toward cleaner and more consistent video quality.
  - Reduced unnecessary quality degradation during gameplay.
  - Streaming changes are designed to preserve DroidLink's low-latency performance.

- **Connection Reliability**
  - Improved session cleanup when players disconnect.
  - Better handling of returning to the main menu after a session.
  - General WebRTC and connection stability improvements.

- **UI & Quality-of-Life Improvements**
  - Continued interface cleanup and polish.
  - Improved session/player information.
  - Removed or reduced unnecessary diagnostic information from normal use.
  - General usability improvements throughout the app.

- **Under-the-Hood Improvements**
  - Additional stability fixes and code cleanup.
  - Improved handling of longer gaming sessions.
  - Continued preparation for future Android/device compatibility.
  - No unnecessary changes to systems that are already working reliably.

### Current Goal

DroidLink is getting closer to its stable release target. Development is now increasingly focused on **polish, reliability, video quality, long-session stability, and future-proofing** rather than rebuilding systems that already work.

Thank you to everyone testing DroidLink and helping identify issues.

**Connect. Stream. Play.**

# 🚀 DroidLink v3.0

DroidLink 3.0 is here! 🎮🟢

- Improved remote physical controller support
- Increased controller stability during longer gaming sessions
- Improved input handling across supported games and emulators
- Reduced chances of controllers disconnecting or becoming unresponsive mid-game
- Continued improvements to Player 2 remote input

### ⚡ Streaming & Latency
- Further latency optimizations for a more responsive gaming experience
- Improved streaming stability between Android devices
- Smoother handling of active DroidLink sessions
- Connection improvements designed to keep gameplay responsive

### 🖥️ UI & Experience

- Cleaner Host and Join workflow
- Improved fullscreen behavior while gaming

### 🛠️ Under the Hood
- General bug fixes
- Performance optimizations
- Controller reliability improvements
- Streaming stability improvements
- Code cleanup and preparation for future DroidLink features

## ⚠️ Beta Software

DroidLink is still actively being developed and tested.

Different Android devices, networks, games, emulators, and controllers may behave differently. If you find a bug, please report what device, emulator/game, and controller you were using.

## 🔮 What’s Next?

Development will continue on:

- Broader emulator/controller compatibility
- Streaming and latency improvements
- Audio improvements
- UI customization
- Controller testing tools
- Additional multiplayer features
- More DroidLink quality-of-life improvements

Thank you to everyone testing DroidLink and helping improve it. 💚

# DroidLink v2.7 — Performance & Stability Update 🎮⚡

DroidLink **v2.7** is focused on combining the controller stability achieved in v2.6 with the faster, more responsive streaming performance of earlier builds.

## 🚀 What's New

### ⚡ Improved Streaming Latency

* Major focus on reducing host-to-player delay.
* Restored and refined low-latency optimizations from the highly responsive **2.0 v2** build.
* Reduced unnecessary frame buffering and stale-frame buildup.
* Improved responsiveness during fast-paced gameplay.
* Better long-session latency consistency.

### 🎮 Stable PC / Winlator Controls

* Preserves the major controller stability improvements introduced in **v2.6**.
* Controllers are designed to remain connected throughout longer gaming sessions.
* Improved reliability of buttons, analog sticks, triggers, and Start input.
* Controller stability was protected while latency improvements were introduced.

### 🕹️ PS2 Controller Stability

* Existing stable PS2 controller support remains intact.
* Changes were designed to avoid interfering with the already-working PS2 input path.

### 🎨 UI Improvements

* UI color customization remains available.
* Choose between **Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, and Purple** themes.
* Improved Online/Offline connection-status behavior.
* Existing fullscreen and in-session menu behavior preserved.

### 🔐 Security

* Existing DroidLink security protections remain enabled.
* Performance improvements were implemented without intentionally removing security safeguards.

## 🧪 Current Focus

v2.7 is an important foundation release for DroidLink.

The goal was simple:

**v2.6 Controller Stability + 2.0 v2 Low Latency = v2.7**

With the PC/Winlator and PS2 foundations becoming more stable, development can begin expanding reliable controller support to additional emulators.

### 🔜 Coming Next: GameCube / Dolphin

The next major controller target is **GameCube support through Dolphin**, while keeping the stable PC/Winlator and PS2 controller paths protected.

Thanks to everyone testing DroidLink and reporting issues. Every test helps move the app closer to a stable, low-latency Android-to-Android gaming experience.

**DroidLink v2.7 — Stable controls. Lower latency. More platforms coming.**

Build verification:
- :app:testDebugUnitTest passed
- :app:assembleDebug passed

Physical-device security, streaming, and controller verification is still required.

Droid Link 1.1

What’s new:

- Added improved host game-audio capture, RTP, playout, and routing diagnostics
- Added adaptive video bitrate, frame-rate, and resolution controls aimed at lower latency and reduced choppiness
- Added optional two-way voice chat with Opus, microphone permission, mute, receive, and volume controls
- Added AEC, noise suppression, and gain-control capability diagnostics
- Expanded session diagnostics for video bottlenecks, audio packet flow, and voice activity
- Preserved the Droid Link 1.0 WebRTC, controller, and session baseline

Testing status:

- Debug build; physical-device verification is required
- Voice Chat defaults OFF and only requests microphone access when enabled
- Android game-audio capture availability can vary by device and by the game’s capture policy
- Headphones are recommended while testing voice chat
- Droid Link 1.0 remains available as the stable rollback release

name: BROKEN — DO NOT INSTALL — Droid Link 1.0
body:
> [!WARNING]
> **BROKEN — DO NOT INSTALL.** This APK uses obsolete Firebase/TURN server configuration and cannot connect reliably. Install [DroidLink v3.6](https://github.com/Aihoward/DroidLink/releases/tag/v3.6). Existing installations must be replaced with v3.6.

Droid Link 1.0

Droid Link allows Android devices and gaming handhelds to connect directly for low-latency game streaming and remote multiplayer.

Highlights:

- Android-to-Android game streaming
- Remote game audio
- DroidLink Player 2 virtual controller
- Winlator controller support
- PS2/emulator multiplayer support
- Low-latency controller transport
- Adaptive WebRTC video streaming
- Direct P2P with TURN fallback
- Real-state pre-game readiness check
- Bounded reconnect recovery with clear retry actions
- Connection Stats and advanced diagnostics
- Neon black/green UI and session controls
- Automatic session and controller cleanup
- Controller diagnostics and streaming presets

This is the first stable Droid Link release.

Known limitations:

- This APK is debug-signed because no private release-signing configuration is stored in the project
- Android playback-audio capture availability depends on the host app and device
- Virtual Player 2 creation requires compatible device access/permissions
- Network and hardware performance vary by device
- Voice chat, accounts, matchmaking, and Players 3/4 are not included

- Improved Connection Stats and session menu presentation

- No per-frame Compose state is used for the background
- Existing renderer, media tracks, DataChannels, and PeerConnection remain alive behind session overlays

Known beta status:

- This remains a beta/debug build
- Physical-device regression and long-session testing are required before 1.0
- Android playback-audio capture support varies by app and device
